by_deadline.rule: a device answer counts only if it arrived by the 2.0 s single-shot deadline. refspatial device completion is p50 1.9947 s against that deadline and 126 of 1,042 measured single-shot questions exceed it, all of them refspatial (45.5 percent of that dataset); realworldqa has none.

assistive_value.cloud_side_unscored: the cloud's SS answers are recorded but NOT scored in this function; scoring them needs each benchmark's own scorer from experiments/casestudy/ss2_kit.py. standing_accuracy over cloud-served opportunities is therefore absent, not zero.
assistive_value.metrics_not_comparable: refspatial point_accuracy and realworldqa exact_match are DIFFERENT metrics and are never averaged together here

caveats: D85: dashcam task value is streaming AP over the clip-PLAYS completed in the run, indexed by play id and paired across arms. It is NOT comparable to the committed 300-clip AP. D84: repeated clips or sessions across devices are separate plays and are NOT independent samples.

D87: robot device answers are the 4B-I x RECENT set of StudyO-Q4 (845 questions, 32.78 %), restricted to EVAL. They were produced by the 4B on the A6000 / H100, NOT on the Orin. StudyD15 Part A rejected the H100-for-Orin proxy as an exact numerical stand-in, so these answers are valid for ordering and first-order value, not as exact device numbers.

D70: the wire format is JPEG. S-EMBER q88 parity is NOT proven within the pre-registered +/- 2 pp rule (K3 +0.83 pp [-0.24, +2.01], K1 -0.6 pp with lower bound -2.14, about 6 % of letters change). S-EMBER cloud accuracy here is the cloud's actual answers on JPEG input.

D81: vLLM's prefix-cache path is not output-identical to recompute (StudyORIN3 Part 2: first-token drift p50 0.22, max 0.45 nats; 39 / 40 answers agree). Robot accuracy is reported split WARM / COLD from the request log's cache_path.
score.on_time_rule: an answer is delivered at COMPLETION, prefill plus decode (D146, the default from 2026-11-20); a dashcam Yes/No stays at first token

partial.trace_meta_stand_in: NOT the capture-time trace_meta.json, which is not committed and whose frozen-grid working copy is the H100's disk (committed d192_device_scores_provenance.json). The knobs are the committed D192 provenance for this trace; seed / n_devices / ratio / run_s / mode are this run's own run_meta.json. No fairness digest is placed here: fabricating one would make score.load's digest check compare a value written by this script, so the check is left SKIPPED and the capture-time record (run_meta.digests_equal and fairness_digest == trace_fairness_digest) is asserted above instead.
partial.why: the absent fields are the only ones that read Loaded.records (trace.jsonl) or the calibration map. trace.jsonl and trace_meta.json for this trace are not committed and the frozen-grid working copy is the H100's disk, per the committed d192_device_scores_provenance.json. They are left ABSENT rather than filled from a stand-in trace. The dashcam streaming AP for this cell is still owed and must come from a box that holds the trace.

device_delivery_rule.answer_length: D146 (1) / P20: a robot answer is 2 OUTPUT TOKENS (completion_tokens == 2 on all 97 measured questions), so the 512-token answer cap is not the device's latency lever and a 0.270 s completion is almost entirely prefill plus fixed overhead.

score_refused_pre_d226_3.error: ScoringRefused: D226: 1 delivered cloud answer(s) in covex-v6-fair-final_n16_s4_1200s_h27_3t_kv0.5r_L3_epg_rq30 have request ids absent from the request log (10174 rows); their refusal status is unverifiable and keeping them risks a silent mis-score. First few: ['r10175']
score_refused_pre_d226_3._what: THE PREVIOUS CONTENT OF THIS CELL'S `score` BLOCK, kept verbatim so a reader can see that this cell was once refused and why. The refusal came from the PRE-D226 (3) guard, which stopped on any delivered cloud answer whose request id had no request-log row. D226 (3) (user rule 2026-11-24) replaced that stop with a three-way classification read from the OUTCOME, and the committed scorer KEEPS such an answer when it carries a real delivery.
score_refused_pre_d226_3._why_the_refusal_was_wrong: The one answer it named, r10175, is a genuine delivery: kind=recall on device asst001, cloud_letter 'A' (a real letter, not the 'X' no-letter sentinel), t_opportunity 1199.285107 -> t_cloud_done 1199.962219 -> t_delivered 1199.984395, so cloud compute time was 0.677112 s against the 0.017 s D175 refusal signature, and within_L is true at a 2.0 s deadline. A refusal cannot carry a completion stamp. Its absence from the request log is a WRITER defect at the end of the run, not a refusal: the request log holds exactly r1..r10174 with no gaps, r10175 is the next id, and this run's own run_meta.json records n = 10178 submitted requests, so the last four request-log rows were never flushed before the 1200 s run ended.
